messages:
Matt: Heads-up, saw a big GPU node churn spike in us-west-2 last night. Lots of tiny nodes created instead of packing onto our p3/p4 nodepools. Cost up ~18% on that cluster.
Anya: saw the same in staging earlier today. Pods Pending because nodeSelector/instanceTypes didn't match and we had ENI errors in k8s events.
Sam: do we have karpenter controller logs showing why it preferred new nodes?
Matt: log excerpt: 
```
I0421 23:14:12.101 binding.go:45] binding pod default/train-job-22 to node karpenter-10-0-5-101
E0421 23:14:17.327 aws_provisioner.go:176] launch failed: AssignPrivateIpAddresses: address limit exceeded for subnet subnet-0a1b2c3d
I0421 23:14:42.900 provisioner.go:104] created node ip-10-0-5-112 (p3.8xlarge) providerID: aws:///us-west-2/i-0f12e34ab
```
Kevin: ENI / subnet IP exhaustion is the smoking gun. If kubelet max-pods is too high vs ENI attachments, nodes look full and karpenter will create more.
Lia: checking our provisioner manifest, consolidation was removed in a revert last week. That probably prevented GC.
Anya: current provisioner we applied: 
```
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: "karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family"
      operator: In
      values: [ "p3", "p4" ]
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 3600
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: kubernetes-usw2
    securityGroupSelector:
      kubernetes.io/cluster: redwood-prod
```
Sam: so consolidation:false + long ttl = fragmentation. Karpenter keeps nodes around and ENI limits get hit.
Matt: short-term mitigations?
Kevin: open an AWS ENI/subnet quota increase & expand subnet capacity (support ticket). Update LaunchTemplate so kubelet max-pods matches ENI limits for each instance type.
Anya: also prefer larger instances in instanceTypes so we end up with fewer nodes: prefer p4d -> p4 -> p3. And for critical training, use capacityTypes: ["on-demand"] to avoid spot churn.
Lia: propose a canary: enable consolidation:true, ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 900, instanceTypes prioritized, add subnet free-IP preflight, run 48h canary in staging with synthetic GPU workloads.
Sam: test plan: submit 200 concurrent GPU pods (varied sizes) and monitor provision latency, ENI errors, consolidation events, and cost delta.
Matt: I'll own the manifest change and rollout. infra-qa runs the load test.
Kevin: I'll PR LaunchTemplate tweaks to set kubelet max-pods appropriately and add capacityTypes preference. Note: our current LT user-data has: 
```
#cloud-config
kubelet:
  kubeletArguments:
    max-pods: [ 110 ]
```
We need to set per-instance-family values (eg 58 for p3.8xlarge).
Anya: add a CI preflight script to fail the canary if subnet free IPs or ENI quota below threshold.
Lia: infra-qa will collect metrics and build a dashboard: node churn, ENI errors, GPU spend. Also add a cost alert if daily GPU spend >10% baseline.
Matt: immediate action items: 
- Matt: draft provisioner manifest (consolidation + ttl + instanceTypes) by EOD
- Anya: open AWS ENI/subnet quota request + add infra CI quota check (today)
- Kevin: PR LaunchTemplate changes (max-pods, capacityTypes)
- infra-qa: prepare synthetic GPU load job and dashboards
- Sam: test harness + gating tests for scheduling/taints/affinity
Kevin: suggest blacklisting older GPU families (g4) in canary only. They cause longer job times and more preemptions.
Anya: agree keep blacklist in canary for now.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0819 - ENI quota causing provisioning churn. Linked PR: infra/karpenter/389.
Matt: timeline: canary start 09:00 PT tomorrow. Check at 24h, decision at 48h. Keep nodepools as rollback path.
Lia: :thumbsup: I'll collate logs and timelines for the canary. Ping me for any specific node traces.
Sam: I'll post the harness instructions and a short runbook for rollback.
Anya: I'll add the subnet/ENI query script to infra tools.
Matt: Thanks all. I'll open the PR and tag reviewers @Anya @Kevin @Lia.
